I didn't touch this game until 2021 because I thought it was dead at launch.
My concerns were quashed when the devs revealed the total number of accounts made had surpassed 6 million.
I have had no problem finding matches and the hub world is always packed full of player avatars.
The thing that really sold me on this game was the character customization, it's surprisingly good.

Only gripe would be the lack of maps; They all become repetitive very fast.

TL;DR The game has many unique features that other Naruto games lack and has many satisfying parts of it's gameplay loop. However, the game suffers from poor map variety, DLC locked moves(although inexpensive), and a clothing system that could be reworked to allow more accessibility. 

!! BUY THE GAME + DLCs ON SALE !!

This game has given me many fun filled hours, many opportunities to make new friends, and checks many boxes I wish were in other Naruto games. As long as you're running a decent PC, you will encounter little or no graphical or technical issues. 
The customization in the game is great, allowing you to truly craft a character you love in the series or one of your own, although it could use some more options when it comes to body sizes and facial features(for example, there are only 2-3 beards). 
The combat is satisfying to take part in, and you really feel some accomplishment when you learn how to consistently make combos with each of the classes unique weapons. There is a great variety of jutsu you can use, unfortunately many of them are locked behind DLCs, although inexpensive. The developers try to balance each move to make them useable, but be aware that not all of them will be best. 
The Map variety is very small, consisting of only 4 maps for teammodes, and only 1 for the free for all gamemode. There isn't really anything special about the maps either, so they come off as boring and non-substantial. 
Finally, the clothing system could use some work. Many of the more unique outfits are locked behind rewards for participating in prior leagues, many of which take a long time to reappear. While this keeps certain outfits and items rare, it leads many to mod their characters to unlock everything in the game(alongside set them at the max level, which doesn't give any benefits, but still takes away the reward of getting there yourself). 

As a final note: Hackers are currently a problem in the game. While modders give themselves all the items, it ultimately doesn't hurt anyone. Hackers, on the other hand ruin the game for everyone and actively make people not want to play the game. The developers have done precious little to contain it, and I'm not sure how far they will go to defend against it in the future. All we can do is wait for them to get bored and report them.

I'm a long-time Naruto fan, and when I heard rumblings of this game back when, I was slightly excited, to have the opportunity to create my own ninja, and share a world with my favorite characters, doing missions with my friends and things of the sort. After I've learned what the game was and what it included, my excitement waned until it vanished completely. So after waiting for this game to go on sale and playing through most of what the game has to offer, these are my thoughts.

If you're hoping for an epic Naruto story that revolves around your development as a ninja, don't. This game has no real coherent story, as you're introduced into the game and made your character, you'll be greeted with a boring dialogue that introduces you to the world and it's facilities where you'll do your missions, PVE, PVP, customization and all that. After that small introduction you're on your own. While the gameplay itself is fun, the missions are repetitive and get boring eventually, being redeemed only when you do them with friends. The missions offer no real story and just serve as a platform for you to level up, get scrolls (that net you customization items, like loot crates), and advance your master level which gives you all sorts of rewards.

Now, in the customization part, I was very disappointed, with the lack of optional clothes and original content, what's the point of making my own ninja if 85% of the customization items are based on the original characters, like don't get me wrong, it's cool to look like them, I just wish there were more options for individuality, and this goes for hair-types, Jutsus (which is alright, I guess) and "make-up". In addition, something that really annoyed me is the recoloring of outfits, and by recoloring I don't mean you get to pick from a palette of colors or a slide system, oh no, they have made original palettes with color combinations that they chose, and let me tell you, I'm not exaggerating when I'm saying that the choices they give are some of the worst color combination I have ever seen, ugly can't even begin to describe them, so most of the time, you'll find yourself sticking to the original palettes as they look the best. Not only that, they added *some* differentiation to the costumes, adding ugly-ass patterns to already existing outfits, there's really nothing to look for when obtaining these items from scrolls and you're better off just earning cash to buy what you want straight up from the store.

Now I know, there's season two yet to come, but I don't really see them adding anything original apart from more "masters" and a couple of missions, another lazy thing is, at first I had the idea that you would've picked your village at the beginning of the game and start there as you go through the villages for different missions. Nope, you get one boring and small map of Konoha, I can't even call it a map, it's pretty much a tiny lobby, where you can't jump on top of buildings, can't interact with almost anything, it's just bland and boring. The animations for walking around in the lobby are horrible, like the adventure mode in Bandai's Naruto games, and I guess it shouldn't surprise me that they've essentially ripped them from the games, while the game itself is graphically inferior to those games in every aspect.

Overall, this game is disappointing, and as someone who hates live-service games, I guess I should've known, but my love for Naruto got the better of me this time, with the anime and manga ending, and Boruto being sub-par, who knows when and if we'll get decent games in the future.

As a long-time fan of Naruto, this game is fun to... only a certain extent. I'm not the biggest fan of open PVP battle royales, and I got into this game mostly because I was attracted to the idea of playing a Naruto game where I could make my own character and play with my friends online. I knew that this game would have open PVP as a large portion of its gameplay, but I was hoping there would at least have some kind of decent story mode outside of that. Well... turns out there really isn't. The only story mode this game has is doing a set of standard missions in the "Ninjutsu VR Arena", and then doing it again but with a higher difficulty. And then again, but with an even higher difficulty. And then that's it, all that's left to do in the game is to replay the missions or by doing the PVP. The missions that we get as "training" are fun, but it's not fun to keep doing the same missions over and over again "but this time it's harder". After a while, it just gets boring and repetitive. It's extra frustrating because the concept of the Ninjutsu VR Arena is extraordinarily cool, and I feel like it has a lot of potential as a major plot point in what could have been an epic and sprawling MMORPG storyline. But there isn't one, and that means the Ninjutsu VR Arena feels like missed potential once its temporary purpose has been served.

On top of that, this game is FULL of broken DLC and horrible gambling mechanics. The shop has some items that you can buy with free in-game currency, but if you want to get your hands on any of the event items or more uncommon clothing and accessories, you'll have to gamble to get it. The gambling is frustrating too because regardless of what gender character you play you'll get clothing that you cannot wear because all the outfits are gender-locked and you have a chance to gain clothing that isn't for your gender. And ON TOP OF THAT, all the extra rare event items have HORRIBLE drop rates. You can drop tons of dollars on moonlight scrolls and not get anything after spending all of them on the gatcha machines. It's the WORST.

Oh, and remember that broken DLC I mentioned before? There's plenty of DLC for new VR Masters that you can train under so you can learn their jutsu forms, but some of the DLC promises moonlight scrolls when you buy it, and you'll not see any of those scrolls in your inventory once you buy them. Sometimes the DLC descriptions feel misleading or unnecessarily confusing, and you'll end up buying something that feels like it should be a bundle for a set of masters only for you to get something entirely different once you buy it.

It's frustrating, because I really want to like this game. In fact I do, but again, only to some extent. I have fun playing alongside my friends, but I simply do not want to deal with the PVP elements, and that's half of the gameplay. There really aren't any other Naruto games on the market with good character creators AND online co-op modes, this is all we have, and that seriously sucks.

All my complaining aside, TLDR; just make sure you know what you're getting into with this game. If you like battle royales and competitive PVP, then I'm sure you'll have a blast, but if you're getting into this game hoping it'll have a fun MMORPG style story, then you're probably going to be disappointed.

Naruto: Xenoverse, this is not.

For what it's worth: What IS there is quite solid and could form the foundation of a genuinely good game. The problem is - there's very little there.

First off, the single-player experience is unfun at *best*. It consists of the same 5 or 6 missions repeated at higher and higher difficulties until finally the credits roll, and there's nothing to them. Just spam buttons until the mission is over, and don't worry about dying because your only "lives" are the time limit, which you have plenty of time in every mission to finish.

But of course, the main draw of this game is the multiplayer, so it doesn't lose that much for the single player. However, the player vs CPU just consists of more of the same missions over and over, just with 3 other human players with you. And what's worse is, as much of an afterthought these PvE missions are, you're REQUIRED to do them to actually unlock all the trainers that you have to go through to unlock more skills.

As for the PvP...it exists. A grand total of 5 maps, with 4 gamemodes, 2 of which are locked in quick play and *3* are locked in ranked. The skills are all basically the same exact thing from a small selection of skill types, there's no matchmaking whatsoever, some skills are downright broken...again, the poor single player is excuseable because that's not the main draw of this game, but to compensate the multiplayer needs to *actually be good itself*, and it's not.

Even character creation just amounts to "how tall do you want to be?" and "pick from a selection of very slightly different faces". There's no interesting outfits, nothing new to the game itself, every outfit is just the clothes from a canon character, and even that selection is relatively small

Again, what is there is good - mechanically things are smooth, for the most part. Traversing maps with wall running and super jumping is easy and enjoyable, but you can't have a good game with just the foundation. I've seen game betas with more, and more varied, content than this

You have your light/heavy attacks, two jutsu for abilities, ninja tools to help you and or your team survive, you can kinda make builds so-to-speak, and so on. It's basically something like Paladins or Overwatch, but it's a fighting game.

The controls in my personal experience took me a bit to get used to, but they're not bad at all. The one complaint I do have is the blocking/dashing mechanic. If you want to block, you have to make sure you are standing still, not moving your character at all. Pressing the block button while moving will execute a dash. In general games, when moving, pressing the block button will make your character block right on the dime, while dashing is executed by pressing block twice whilst moving your thumbstick to your desired location, or maybe tapping the thumbstick whilst blocking. How blocking/dashing in this game works is unnecessarily difficult. Not to mention I feel like dashing doesn't have enough invisibility frames and it doesn't travel far enough. Also on that note, the lock-on system. Again, comparing to other games, when facing an enemy which your camera is focused on, you should automatically lock onto the next enemy after defeating that one. After you defeat one in this game, you'd have to turn your camera and spot the enemy who is still within your range and possibly is going to get the first hits in on you since you'd have to re-lock to that enemy. This game has a lot of potential, & I have to say, it's amazingly fun. Except....it has a LOT of problems. 

First off; the game's balancing needs work. Like, excessive amounts. It is way too easy to spam attacks, and some classes for some reason get skills that make them infinitely, excessively more powerful than the other classes. Specifically, the Attack & Range classes get most of the moves from the masters. Defense classes get nowhere near as much in terms of usable skills as the attack classes, and ranged class gets moves that can be spammed to the point of game-breaking strength from level one.

Attack class' skills are also extremely overpowered, able to ragdoll you to death so fast the Flash would wonder 'what the heck just hit me?'

On top of that, there's the DLCs. The DLC masters can be used freely with levelup, but they only give you skills(or literally anything other than the ability to play as them) if you buy said DLCs, and said DLC skills are MASSIVELY overpowered, moreso than most skills in the basegame, making the game Pay-to-Win.

Apart from skill issues, the game is peer-to-peer in battle servers, meaning you will find lag. a. lot. And i'm still half-convinced that 90% of it is artificial, used by other players to give themselves an edge.

There's also the problem that the voice chat systems don't work properly, and that's only when they work at all. The menu chat systems are almost as bad, being so minimalistic they're basically useless.

So, to sum it all up; This game has amazing potential, but it's ruined by the game's lag issues, lack of any even remotely proper balancing, lack of properly-built communication systems, and pay-to-win tendencies.

If you can stomach going into a battle and finding yourself dead in ten seconds flat because every other player does nothing but use the most broken, unbalanced, overpowered skills in the game, some of which they probably bought their way to instead of earning it via hard work, by all means, you'll enjoy this game. Otherwise, don't buy it. It'll save you money, as well as stop you from breaking your keyboard via pure frustration.

A fun and competitive team-based fighting game based in the Naruto world. There is a decent roster of characters to choose from, each with their own set of jutsus that you can integrate into your own. The combat is fast-paced and movement-oriented, but it can feel clunky at first. The learning curve is steep, but it gets really fun once you get used to it.

There are 4 different game modes for multiplayer PvP, and they rotate each season on a bi-weekly basis. There is also a solo/co-op set of missions you can do if you want to get certain jutsus first before touching PvP. However, they are not as interesting as the PvP modes.

Equipment matters, and the best ones are locked behind a gacha. However, you can easily farm the currency used (scrolls) by playing a lot. The game lacks polish in some areas, but overall, it's a decent Naruto game. The only downside it has no matchmaking so prepare to fight against group of sweaty players and it crashes a lot. A LOT. 

If you are a fan of the franchise, I would recommend getting it on sale.

[b]Pros:[/b]
[b]+[/b] There is a character creator and this is your character.
[b]+[/b] A decent amount of Jutsu to learn and use for combat.
[b]+[/b] Some difference in melee fighting styles.

If you notice that it seems vague...Well, this is why...

[b]Cons:[/b]
[b]-[/b] Heavily PVP focused. If you are walking into this looking for a more narrative experience like Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, then go elsewhere.
[b]-[/b] There is a character creator, but it feels hollow and uninspired. Character Customization, with gear unlocked even at twelve hours in feels like a joke.
[b]-[/b] The melee fighting styles are all tied to what I will just call 'Class Types' and are almost all useless. The only one that feels like you should ever be in melee is the bare knuckles for the assaulter/attacker type of character. If you're support, you can't do that. They are so lackluster that if you're in melee you're already doing it wrong in most cases.
[b]-[/b] There are many Jutsu to use, but there are too many that feel worthless compared to others. Some you will never use, at all, and you will forget even exists.
[b]-[/b] Traversing the map is so-so at best. The wall-running was a good step but the jumping off of them and orienting yourself takes a lot of getting used to.
[b]-[/b] Most combat between teams will hit you at range, gang up on one character, and that's really it. Whoever gangs up first and hardest wins.
[b]-[/b] Aside from the PVP mode there isn't much to it. There are side missions you can do, and you can do them with friends...But they don't feel too great to play and I found myself not wanting to play it more and more often.
[b]-[/b] All instructors are just a choice of who appears on your few missions you do to help you with it and nothing really else. If there is more, there isn't too much more worthwhile.
[b]-[/b] There are missions you can take up in the 'VR Training Area' but there aren't too many and it feels pathetically, laughably shallow. This, done right, could've made this a ton of fun with friends if there were better combat mechanics, bosses to fight, and if the enemies didn't just bum rush you the way that they do for human opponents or just machine gun spam ranged attacks that have knockback, tracking, and wide areas of effect for inhuman ones.
[b]-[/b] Hub 'world' would be a hilariously over-estimation of the hub area. It's uninspired and just feels like they could've done leagues better.

This is what I meant. I may not be the demographic for this game, I may just be a poor fit overall...That said, I can't recommend this game. Even on sale at a lowered price it wasn't worth it as there is too little content to care about it and it feels as though this isn't a completed game or even a decent one.

[b]In conclusion:[/b] If you're looking for a Naruto Fighting Game that is purely PVP look for another Naruto title entirely. You will be happier with the results, I am sure and they might have some single player content that can keep you busy when there's no one to fight.

But if you're an Anime Fan, want a better experience with tighter controls, a semi-decent creator with different ways to fight that feel more unique, special abilities that you can use that can feel impactful in a fight, some REALLY fun Multiplayer, decent world building (provided you look around and talk with NPC's instead of just ignoring them or pay attention to things clearly said in the middle of battle), and a narrative experience that makes you the central character? Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2.
